notes: Cross-vendor decision-model comparison by one practitioner (skill-siujev evidence.md section 5d, closed issue #2): n=200 per public set; fresh mirrors (686 items, written 2026-10-01 by Claude and verified blind by Gemini 3.8 Flash) are NOT stored as rows (many cells are slash-joined multi-set values). Run on 2026-10-01 through OpenRouter from one client in Poland: latency includes the OpenRouter hop. With n=200 Wilson intervals are about +-5 points, so most gaps are noise; the Banking77 lead of d1 (87.5 vs Jev 80.5), Mercury and Kev did NOT survive fresh Banking77-style messages (Jev 99.3, d1 98.7, Mercury 98.0, Kev 96.7), consistent with (but not proof of) training exposure to Banking77. Tev1 4B accepts at most 20 options, Solar Decide at most 26, so they cannot run 77-way Banking77. The secondary digest of ~20 other community benchmarks in the same file was NOT independently fetched and is not stored.

claims.statement: skill-siujev: "The 6–7-point lead that D1, Mercury and Kev had on public Banking77 did not survive fresh messages with the same 77 labels". Fresh results: Jev 99.3, D1 98.7, Mercury 98.0, Kev 96.7; gain from public to fresh: Jev +18.8 and Luna +18.5, against Mercury +11.5, D1 +11.2 and Kev +9.7. Issue #2 summary: "Liquid D1 ... was a statistical tie with Jev on every task except public Banking77, where it was ahead (87.5 vs 80.5, p < 0.01)."
claims.implication: A public-benchmark lead (Banking77) may reflect exposure to the benchmark; test on unpublished items.

claims.statement: skill-siujev: Kev is strongly underconfident (on fresh telecom intents only 20% of answers reach 0.8 although all of those are right); thresholds do not transfer between models.
